framework_instructions.contractualist: Evaluate general principles by their justifiability to affected individuals. A principle may permit multiple actions and an action may be permitted by multiple principles. Form individual, personal reasons expressed in terms available to anyone in a relevantly similar position. Include excluded recipients and involuntary contributors. Tie each personal reason to one individual or generic individual position, one relevant value and the principle/action challenged or supported. These are reconstructed arguments, not reported preferences or speech. Compare objections to alternative principles with explicit grounds and warrants. Neither count reasons nor maximize a minimum welfare score. Do not invent strength weights or assume actual unanimity or that any objection is a veto. Defend which rejections are reasonable or preserve the comparison as unresolved. For risk distinguish ex ante prospects from ex post burdens. An unfulfilled assurance does not by itself establish wrongful betrayal or actual reliance. Construct each option's individual positions before comparing complaints. Keep shared burdens in the comparison; rejecting one option does not justify a different option against every remaining alternative. A provisional preference depends on a defended conditional argument, not on the mere existence of an unresolved comparison. Identifying the critical unanswered questions is a substantive contribution; an action recommendation is NOT required. Do not assume a winner must emerge. When comparative priority is not defended, identify the exact unresolved question, affected individuals, competing principles and available actions. Separate missing facts, disputed interpretations and normative priority: more precise facts alone need not resolve a normative comparison. Explain why the question matters, what evidence or argument could help, and what follows conditionally from different answers. Do not invent a numerical exchange rate between unlike reasons, treat uncertainty as a tie, or let a proposed tie-breaker become justified merely because a decision is wanted. Test the actual competing principles; rejecting an absolute rule does not defeat a qualified opposing principle. Hypothetical acceptance by a reasonable person is a proposed argument, not actual consent, a prediction of majority opinion, or proof that dissent is unreasonable. Do not infer consent from role-play. An open question can be decision-relevant without being answerable on this record. Do not declare it unanswerable in principle or a failure of contractualism. Use a null recommendation and UNRESOLVED when no ranking is justified. A conditional preference is allowed only with its disputed priority premise explicit; it does not resolve the question. A genuinely defended ranking may still support a recommendation. Do not force abstention when independent reasons settle the comparison.
